title: A metabolite-pair controlled quiescence switch via ATP-dependent phase separation
task: Identify metabolite-driven phase separation mechanism controlling cellular quiescence
key_results: NH₄⁺/HCO₃⁻ pair synergistically depletes ATP, triggering selective protein phase separation into RD bodies
ATP restoration fully dissolves condensates and restores growth; initial ATP levels predict awakening times in dormant cells
comments: The hydrotrope mechanism for ATP is elegant, but the generality of RD body protein composition and whether all phase-separated proteins require ATP-hydrotrope activity remains to be fully mapped.

model_io.model: Yeast cells under carbon starvation

hypotheses.hypothesis: ATP acts as a biological hydrotrope to maintain protein solubility independent of hydrolysis
hypotheses.result: ATP depletion permits selective phase separation of growth-related proteins

hypotheses.hypothesis: NH₄⁺/HCO₃⁻-dependent quiescence pathway is conserved across kingdoms
hypotheses.result: Pathway also induces reversible quiescence in yeast, suggesting broad conservation

hypotheses.hypothesis: Initial ATP levels in dormant cells predict reactivation timing
hypotheses.result: Quantitative correlation between ATP concentration and awakening times observed

title: Histological evaluation of pulpal healing following direct pulp capping with polytetrafluoroethylene or melatonin, with or without adjunctive low-level laser therapy in Wistar rat molars
task: Compare efficacy of polytetrafluoroethylene versus melatonin for direct pulp capping with or without low-level laser therapy
key_results: MEL + LLLT group showed greatest dentin bridge thickness (~150 μm at 4 weeks) and reduced inflammation scores; LLLT-treated groups demonstrated 2-3 fold improvement in odontoblast layer organization versus controls
comments: The study demonstrates adjunctive benefit of LLLT in pulpal healing, but lacks quantitative inflammatory scores and statistical comparisons across all groups.

model_io.model: Wistar rat maxillary first molars with standardized pulp exposure
inputs: LLLT (650 nm, 100 mW, 11.9 J/cm²) on alternate days

hypotheses.hypothesis: LLLT improves pulpal healing outcomes independent of capping material

hypotheses.hypothesis: Melatonin + LLLT combination produces superior pulpal healing versus other treatments
hypotheses.result: Supported; MEL + LLLT demonstrated the most favorable overall histological profile

title: Glucocorticoids directly inhibit insulin biosynthesis via the glucocorticoid receptor in pancreatic β-cells
task: Determine direct glucocorticoid effects on insulin biosynthesis in pancreatic β-cells
key_results: Dexamethasone reduced Ins1/Ins2 expression and glucose-stimulated insulin secretion (GSIS) by ~50%; GR or JNK inhibition reversed these defects
comments: The finding that GR/JNK inhibition can protect β-cells from steroid-induced dysfunction has therapeutic potential, though the disconnect between in vivo GSIS preservation and in vitro GSIS reduction warrants clarification.

model_io.model: C57BL/6J mice treated with corticosterone or dexamethasone
MIN6 pancreatic β-cell line with GR antagonist, JNK inhibitor, or GR knockdown

hypotheses.hypothesis: Glucocorticoids directly suppress insulin biosynthesis via GR signaling
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; GR antagonism or knockdown ameliorated dexamethasone-induced reductions in insulin gene expression and GSIS

hypotheses.hypothesis: JNK pathway is downstream of GR in mediating insulin biosynthesis suppression
hypotheses.result: Supported; JNK inhibition preserved insulin granule density and reversed gene expression changes

title: PSMD14 reduced microglial M2 polarization to promote ferroptosis and aggravate traumatic brain injury through the induction of BMP6/SMAD3 pathway
task: Elucidate PSMD14 role in traumatic brain injury via microglial ferroptosis and BMP6/SMAD3 signaling
key_results: PSMD14 knockdown increased M2 microglia (IL-10/CD206+) by ~3-fold, reduced pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL-6, TNF-α) by ~60%, and decreased brain pathological injury; PSMD14 activates BMP6/SMAD3 to promote ferroptosis
comments: The mechanistic linkage between PSMD14-driven ferroptosis and microglial polarization is novel; however, the causal relationship between ferroptosis and M2 polarization could be more directly demonstrated.

model_io.model: TBI mouse model with PSMD14 knockdown via shRNA
Microglia isolated from TBI brain tissue

hypotheses.hypothesis: PSMD14 overexpression aggravates TBI by suppressing M2 microglial polarization
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; PSMD14 knockdown shifted microglia toward M2 phenotype and reduced pro-inflammatory cytokines

hypotheses.hypothesis: PSMD14 promotes microglial ferroptosis via BMP6/SMAD3 pathway activation
hypotheses.result: Supported; PSMD14 elevated ROS, mitochondrial damage, and BMP6/SMAD3 signaling, consistent with ferroptotic induction

hypotheses.hypothesis: Behavioral interventions altering social norms can permanently shift epidemic dynamics

title: Maximum likelihood reconstruction of particle trajectories in turbulent flows via sparse optimization
